newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: VENEZUELA DENIES OVERPRODUCING, SAYS AT OPEC QUOTA.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA DENIES OVERPRODUCING, SAYS AT OPEC QUOTA.

text.p: Venezuelan oil minister Erwin Arrieta on Thursday denied reports that his country was producing above its OPEC-assigned output quota.

Asked by reporters if he had admitted to fellow ministers that his country was pumping in excess of its 2.359 million barrels per day (bpd) quota by some 800,000 bpd, as a Gulf source on Wednesday claimed he did, Arrieta denied it.
Asked if his country was producing at its quota he replied: "Yes".
He said Venezuela was producing within 10,000 to 20,000 bpd of its quota.

Saudi Arabia's Ali bin Ibrahim al-Naimi, asked if he was happy with members' commitment to adhere to their quotas after yesterday's decision to freeze the group's 25.033 million bpd ceiling for the rest of the year, said: "We must be happy with that".
OPEC President Abdullah Salem al-Badri, the Libyan oil minister, said that OPEC would be attending to administrative matters today and hoped the next meeting would be held in Jakarta.
Arrieta said that Iran had requested that OPEC meets in Iran's Caspian region in June 1997.
The full OPEC ministerial session was scheduled for 0800 GMT.
